sources.name: Anthony Raines
sources.quote: As a rising name in Rockridge, I've gotten used to people knowing who I am and what I do. It's not something I think about much anymore, to be honest. I just do my job and try to be a good neighbor. I've lived here long enough that it's just part of the fabric of my life. People will sometimes stop me at the corner store or mention something about my stories, and that's nice. It's a good feeling to be recognized for the work you do, especially when it's for something you care about as much as I do about the A's. Benji Dillon's still the big name around here, though - he's a Rockridge icon. I've had some great conversations with him about the community and the team.

sources.name: Benji Dillon
sources.quote: Anthony Raines is a friend, and I'm happy to see him covering the A's. He's got a good eye for the game, and his writing does justice to the team. It's nice having him around Rockridge; we chat about the A's whenever we run into each other.

sources.name: Vinnie Keane
sources.quote: To be honest, I haven't heard much about Anthony Raines around Grand Lake. I know he's a journalist covering the A's, and I've seen his name pop up in the sports feed. I'm still getting used to not being on the field every day, so I don't really know him personally, but it sounds like he's making a name for himself in the sports scene.

sources.name: Lena Cross
sources.quote: To be honest, I haven't heard much about Anthony Raines, but I did notice his name isn't familiar around Piedmont Ave yet. I mean, I've seen some new faces around, and the A's are always a hot topic, so maybe he's getting some buzz in certain circles. I haven't really had a chance to meet him or hear him on the air, but Wendell Carter Jr. is friends with some of the A's players, so maybe I'll learn more through him.
